title: PolarWave Systems — Renewal & Expansion Roadmap
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer evaluating committed capacity increase + EU private deployment pilot for latency/residency. Discussed perf/cost tradeoffs, KMS and SOC2 questions, pilot timeline, pricing amendment. Agreed next steps: security packet, updated pricing, benchmark run w/ sample traffic, and pilot kickoff date proposals.
topics: EU Private / VPC onboarding and data residency
Latency vs cost — quantization and batching tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send updated committed-capacity pricing + EU private addon by 2026-01-14
SE to schedule a 2-hour benchmark run with PolarWave test traffic week of 2026-01-18
Redwood security docs (SOC2, ISO statements, KMS/HSM integration guide) to be shared by 2026-01-12
PolarWave to confirm pilot scope and preferred pilot start date by 2026-01-16
action_items: Ava Thompson: prepare pricing amendment draft for 6-month uplift incl. EU private SKU - due 2026-01-14
Liam Chen: organize benchmark run and share test harness repo + network checklist - due 2026-01-13
Marta Ruiz: provide sample inference traces and P95 latency targets for pilot - due 2026-01-15
Emma Lopez: share procurement timeline and PO window for contract amendment - due 2026-01-16
transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-01-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Marta Ruiz (PolarWave, Head of ML); Jon Park (PolarWave, CTO); Priya Singh (PolarWave, SRE); Emma Lopez (PolarWave, Procurement)

[00:00] Ava Thompson: hey everybody, thanks for joining — can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Marta Ruiz: yes loud and clear, thanks Ava.
[00:08] Ava: cool, quick agenda — renewal check, unpack the EU private ask, run through perf / cost options, and agree next steps. if anyone needs to add, shout now.
[00:20] Jon Park: sounds good, we mainly want alignment on timing for a private pilot and committed capacity increase.
[00:25] Liam Chen: hi all, i'll be jumping into the perf and benchmark piece, and i'll follow up with a proposed runbook.
[00:33] Priya Singh: and i'll focus on the networking / VPC requirements side and egress questions.

[02:02] Ava: ok, quick refresh — PolarWave current committed tier is 2 reserved GPU-pools, that covers about 400k tokens/day peak, right Marta?
[02:12] Marta: yeah that's right. our ramp forecast now shows 3x growth over next 6 months so we're looking at at least doubling — maybe tripling capacity, and importantly we need EU data residency for a subset of traffic.
[02:27] Ava: understood. two levers: Dedicated (reserved capacity in hosted infra) vs Redwood Private (VPC / onprem). cost and timeline differ.
[02:35] Emma Lopez: procurement note — if we go private there is a longer procurement window and an extra SOW, so timing's important.

[04:00] Liam: on the technical front, first we should baseline current P95 for the main inference route. Marta, what's the P95 you're seeing now?
[04:10] Marta: currently about 220ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), but for longer RLHF-ish prompts we see 650-800ms. that's on our side, though we think part of that is network hop and tokenization differences.
[04:24] Liam: ok. on Redwood dedicated we can typically keep P95 sub-250ms for short prompts on the same model family — but there are tradeoffs, for example quantized variants drop token cost ~30% but can add 10-20ms tail. continuous batching parameters also change P50/P95.
[04:45] Jon: hmm, so cost savings vs latency spike. for user-facing chat sessions we want <300ms P95 ideally.

[06:10] Ava: do you want a concrete plan — we propose a 6-month amendment: increase to 6 reserved pools with a 20% committed discount, plus an option to run a 4-week EU private pilot to validate residency and latency.
[06:25] Emma: that sounds reasonable. need cost numbers though.
[06:28] Ava: yes i'll send the pricing sheet after the call.

[07:05] Priya: for EU private we need a network checklist — IP allowlist, peering, and cert chain details. also KMS integration is critical: we need to ensure customer-managed keys/patient data never leaves the VPC unencrypted.
[07:20] Liam: we support KMS/HSM via an integration layer; keys can be customer-managed and the control plane only gets artifacts but not cleartext. i'll share the KMS integration doc. caveat: some of our telemetry (metrics/latency) is aggregated and psuedo-anonymized — we'll provide the audit log controls.
[07:42] Marta: do you have SOC2 artefacts? our security team will need it for the SOW.
[07:47] Ava: yes SOC2 type II and ISO statements — we'll attach those and a summary of audit logs and RBAC.

[09:00] Liam: quick perf note — if you want to maintain sub-300 P95 for mixed length traffic, our recommendation is: 1) keep a hot model (non-quantized) on the critical low-latency pool, 2) use a quantized fallback for batchy background workloads, and 3) tune continuous batching thresholds to keep small-request latency low.
[09:20] Marta: can you share numbers? like token cost delta between the hot vs quantized?
[09:25] Liam: roughly speaking, quantized -> 25-35% token cost reduction depending on model and sequence length; tail latency add maybe 10-25ms. i'll put a short table in the bench plan.

[11:12] Jon: what about rollout policies? we have internal canary procedures — can Redwood do model pinning and automatic fallback to hosted when private capacity is saturated?
[11:22] Ava: yes model pinning and policy-based routing are supported. you can pin traffic by route or token-class, and set fallback to hosted or lower-tier model. we'll show the rollout UI in the console if helpful.

[13:05] Priya: network egress costs — who bears egress for cross-region fallbacks?
[13:12] Ava: in the amendment we'll specify egress assumptions; generally customer pays cloud network egress from their VPC; for hosted fallback Redwood covers intra-platform routing — we'll include explicit examples in pricing.

[14:30] Marta: on the timeline, can we do a pilot in EU the week of Jan 25? that gives our infra team time to prep.
[14:36] Emma: procurement may need earlier heads-up, we have a PO window closing Jan 22.
[14:42] Ava: ok — two-pronged: we'll aim to deliver security docs by Jan 12, pricing by Jan 14, and schedule the benchmark run the week of Jan 18. Pilot kickoff week of Jan 25 contingent on PO.

[16:05] Liam: bench run details: 2hr dress rehearsal, 4hr main run with mixed-length traffic (50% short 128 tokens, 30% medium 512 tokens, 20% long 1.5k tokens), capture P50/P95/P99, token cost and GPU utilization. we'll provide the harness and you can run from your VPC to avoid egress surprises.
[16:25] Marta: we'll provide sample traces and a synthetic generator.
[16:30] Liam: great — i'll push the repo link and a dockerized harness. note: small transcriptions — our auto-transcribe sometimes messes up model names, so please name models consistently to avoid confusion.

[18:00] Jon: security aside, our main blocker is procurement timeline + legal review for the amendment. any past customers had fast lanes for EU private?
[18:10] Ava: yes a few Enterprise customers used an expedited SOW template; we'll share that template and you can route through your legal. for the SOW we try to minimize custom clauses to speed review.

[20:05] Marta: two questions from the ML team — 1) will Redwood support stateful chat sessions with KV cache persistence across requests, and 2) how are model version rollbacks handled?
[20:18] Liam: stateful sessions are supported via managed KV cache; you can opt for persistent cache in Private with configurable TTL. rollbacks are via the rollout system — canary, immediate rollback, or gradual percentage shifts. we'll provide the ops playbook.

[22:00] Priya: network port and TLS requirements? we need specifics for firewall rules.
[22:07] Liam: we'll include a one-page network checklist: outbound ports, mutual TLS, certificate chain pinning options. also include the expected IP ranges for the EU nodes.

[24:40] Emma: procurement — can you confirm billing cadence changes if we add a private SKU?
[24:46] Ava: yes, private SKUs are invoiced monthly with the commitment discount applied; we can align invoice dates to your PO window. we'll state that in the pricing amendment.

[26:30] Marta: question on monitoring — will we get token-level cost breakdowns?
[26:34] Ava: yes console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns per route and per token-class. retention settings differ for private vs hosted; we'll note default retention and enterprise retention add-on.

[28:00] Jon: competitor check — we've talked to BigCloud AI and FastServe. BigCloud pushes lower latency but with less transparent token metrics; FastServe has cheaper spot-style pricing but no private deployment. any notes?
[28:14] Ava: that's consistent with our customers' feedback — Redwood focuses on predictable economics + private options; i'll include a short competitor comparison in the package.

[30:20] Liam: for the bench, one more note — please surface any RBAC/SAML groups we should map; we can pre-provision accounts if you give a CSV.
[30:30] Priya: we'll do that.

[32:05] Ava: ok to recap — action items: we'll send security docs by Jan 12, pricing by Jan 14, SE to run bench week of Jan 18, customer to confirm PO/pilot scope by Jan 16. Anything missing?
[32:20] Emma: procurement will need the SOW template and sample invoice — add that to the package.
[32:24] Ava: noted.

[34:00] Marta: slight nuance — we may want to pilot with only a single model family in EU, then expand. can the pilot be scoped that way?
[34:08] Liam: yes absolutely. start narrow (chat model) then roll out to reranking/embeddings. makes the bench cleaner too.

[36:15] Jon: SLA question — do you offer credits for downtime or latency SLO misses?
[36:22] Ava: dedicated plans have SLA credits and we can propose an SLA appendix in the amendment. for private onprem we offer operational runbooks and a support uplift rather than standard SLA credits — we can discuss specifics with Legal.

[38:00] Priya: KMS detail — do you support key rotation without downtime?
[38:06] Liam: yes key rotation is supported with a rolling update key wrap; we'll document exact behavior for your SREs.

[40:10] Ava: ok final check — any blockers to doing the bench and pricing next week?
[40:16] Marta: none on our side if we get the docs and harness early.
[40:20] Emma: procurement just needs the SOW template to start the internal review.
[40:25] Ava: great. we'll ship the package by Jan 12 and follow up with calendar invites for the bench. thanks everyone.
[40:35] Jon: thanks, appreciate it.
[40:38] Marta: thanks, bye.
[40:40] (recording ends)
